destructiveWriterEnumeration.method: A test scans src/ for statements that can set a destructive state (status flips, DELETEs, cell resets) and asserts every module it finds is named in DESTRUCTIVE_WRITERS with a wired flag and a reason. The scan is the control; the register is the answer.

wired.why: wired FIRST, per the dispatch: it is the writer behind both incidents. The tuple the threshold reads is the share of the county's served tier1 population whose record would be stamped retired by this publish, measured BEFORE the bake runs.

registeredNotWired.reason: its population is TWO named place_keys chosen by hand, re-verified live immediately before the delete and already gated by an explicit AUTHORIZATION constant with the card that issued it. A share threshold would be a second, weaker authorisation for a write that has a stronger one. If it ever gains a set-valued mode, it must call assertBlastRadius with the number of rows that mode would delete.

it acts on ONE collision at a time (a pair of rows), so it has no population to take a share of; its control is the collision evidence it is resolving plus a durable run_event written BEFORE the UPDATE.
same shape; it deletes companion rows only, never the served record or its status.

seven rail jobs whose DELETE + re-insert is the same rail's refresh from an acquired source table, bounded by that source's own row count and compared to it by each job's own coverage check; they touch a companion rail, never the served record and never its status.

six cell-rail jobs that overwrite a CELL's state on one rail, driven and bounded by that rail's own source; they never stamp or remove a retirement. This is the group closest to the hazard and the reason is stated at length in the module rather than waved at. A whole-county 'everything not in the source' mode in any of them must call assertBlastRadius.

a second writer to place_layer_snapshots but a VALUES writer: it never stamps a retirement and never nuls a served row, and it refuses a county that is not already served. Its write happens inside an LDT bake subprocess, so the in-repo half is the invocation; its control today is a staging-sibling gate keyed on phase=dollar-fields-patch.

destructiveWriterEnumeration.engineSideNotInThisRepo: P-213's guard (hauska-engine packages/engine-core/scripts/writer-blast-radius-guard.mjs, used by the parcel-node writer) is the same control class in another repo, and A-192 recorded it as the engine's, not the factory's. This lane did NOT port it or modify it, and it did not need to: the engine writer that produced Bastrop already carries it. The factory's guard declares its own threshold and flag because the engine's `maxShare` is supplied per caller there and there is no shared workspace between the repos; the token shape was deliberately matched to the coverage floor's, which is the shape an operator already meets in this repo.

threeQuestionGate.whatExecutesIt: requireRetirementGate / assertBlastRadius, called by runBastropPublish after the coverage floor and before bakesFn for every publish, every target, every county; and runRetiredShareWatch for P-321.
threeQuestionGate.whatTriggersIt: Every publish invocation (P-319/P-320) and every scheduled sweep or --read call (P-321). Nothing is conditional on a flag: the gates run on the ordinary path.
threeQuestionGate.whatFails: PUBLISH_RETIREMENT_KEYSPACE_UNACCOUNTED | PUBLISH_RETIREMENT_UNMEASURED | DESTRUCTIVE_BLAST_RADIUS | DESTRUCTIVE_AUTHORISATION_MALFORMED/MISMATCH/COUNTY_MISMATCH/STALE | RETIRED_SHARE_UNMEASURED | RETIRED_SHARE_TARGET_REQUIRED. On the publish path the refusal propagates before bakesFn, so nothing is written and the bake is never invoked.
whatBypassesIt: A bake run outside runBastropPublish: the LDT conformant CLIs invoked directly (they are separate processes with their own args), and the frozen laptop ingest scripts.
A raw connection or a hand UPDATE that reaches place_layer_snapshots without passing through the publish job. The guard, like the coverage floor, cannot see a write it is not called from.

The retirement the BAKE itself computes, once the bake IS invoked: this repo refuses to invoke it on an unaccounted keyspace, and cannot make the bake's own comparison keyspace-scoped. That is the named, unresolved half of P-319 and it lives in LDT at the pin.
Deleting the gate or catching its throw in a caller: nothing outside the calling job enforces that it is called.

stillOpen: THE UNRESOLVED HALF OF P-319, and the most important line in this close: the retirement is computed in LDT at the pin, so this repo can only refuse to invoke the bake. The bake, when invoked on an ACCOUNTED keyspace, still decides absence by a bare key equality against cad_property -- no crosswalk, and no test that the roll carries the served keyspace. A row in legacy-design-tools should make the bake compute retirement per keyspace and refuse an unaccounted one; until then, the factory's gate is a refusal in front of it, and a bake run outside the publish job bypasses that refusal entirely.

cad_property AT THE DECLARED VINTAGE IS NOT READ BY THIS GATE, and it is the table the retirement's own basis names. P-306 measured 48491's roll as 319,480 numeric accounts AT tax_year 2026 -- so a census of that table would NOT have caught the 2026-09-17 numeric retirements. Any later row that adds that reader must add it as an id-overlap test (or a namespace control), never as a label census, or it will feel like protection without being it.

P-306's own OPEN note (2026-09-17): the 282,569 R-prefixed retirements of 2026-09-10 are 'the same keyspace-mismatch shape as P-212, NOT established as false or correct'. This lane's gate would refuse that shape today (a served keyspace whose every id is absent from the reader), which is a deliberate outcome and not a ruling on whether those retirements are right. The ruling is still owed by someone who can measure it.

P-309's F1-F5 (Hays 846 contradicted CAD-roll-absence retirements; retirement payloads carry no run id; JSON documents in the situs field; the 'PRIVATE ROAD' non-identity node; the P-275 readers' own namespace controls) are untouched by this lane and are the natural input to the P-321 band's first real reading.

The retired-share band's numbers (ceiling 0.9, max move 0.5) were declared from P-309's measured distribution and the incident's own 47 -> 100 percent jump, not from a live series. The first weeks of observations should be read before they are trusted as a control, and the watch records the series for exactly that.
